verdict_text: NO. The merge computes the second task vector against the already-modified intermediate `tmp` instead of the unmodified base: it does `tmp + LAMBDA * (f2 - tmp)` where `tmp = b + LAMBDA * (f1 - b)`, which expands to `b + 0.4*(f1-b) + 0.4*(f2-b) - 0.16*(f1-b)`, not the formula in Required result step 2 (`base + λ(ft1-base) + λ(ft2-base)`). This is exactly the ordering hazard the specification warns about, and the resulting error on the 64 merged tensors will generally exceed the 1e-3 relative Frobenius tolerance since it scales with the size of the ft1 task vector. The shared-tensor verification, merge count, and 244-tensor checks are otherwise present.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
